alternatives.0: No alternative technology or approach is named.
alternatives.1: Names an alternative but cannot say why it was rejected.
alternatives.2: Names at least one real alternative and the decisive difference.
alternatives.3: Compares two or more alternatives on the dimension that actually decided it.

constraints.0: The choice is presented as arbitrary or 'best practice'.
constraints.1: Mentions team size or familiarity without linking it to the decision.
constraints.2: Names the constraints (team, timeline, data shape, deployment target) that narrowed the options.
constraints.3: Explains which constraint was binding and what would change if it disappeared.

costs.0: Claims the choice has no downside.
costs.1: Names a cost only in the abstract ('it can be slower').
costs.2: Names a concrete cost and where it shows up in this codebase.
costs.3: Quantifies or bounds the cost and names the mitigation already in place.

reversibility.0: No sense of how hard the decision is to undo.
reversibility.1: Says it 'could be swapped later' with no analysis.
reversibility.2: Identifies what is coupled to this choice (schemas, queries, deployment).
reversibility.3: Describes the migration path, its blast radius, and whether it can be done incrementally.

hints: Name the alternative you did not pick.
Name the constraint that made the difference a real one.
Say what it would cost to change your mind later.
